rationale: 5 % numeric tolerance for equal-authority supplier variance is consistent with GHS guidance that rounding differences below 5 % do not change hazard category for most physical-hazard thresholds. 0.6 Jaccard for hazard-statement agreement requires that the majority of GHS hazard codes overlap between suppliers before treating their data as consistent; a completely different hazard profile (e.g., one SDS lists H225+H302, another lists H400+H410) would score well below 0.6 and correctly force UNKNOWN.
